A1.justification: Both PDFs describe UNOPose, and all 12 pages of each are readable. However, both reference supplementary or appendix material containing technical details and further experiments that is absent from the supplied files. The supplied main texts support comparison; the referenced material cannot be assessed.

before.justification: V1 reports original segmentation and pose-estimation experiments on LM-O, TUD-L, and YCB-V, including component ablations and reference-rotation analysis.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds coarse-stage overlap-prediction and rendered-reference results in Table 5.

M1.justification: The documented SAM/DINOv2 segmentation and GRF/LRF coarse-to-fine pose pipeline remain unchanged, including overlap weighting, pose selection, losses, and weighted-SVD inference. The added ablations test configurations of the existing method.

E1.justification: MegaPose training data and LM-O, TUD-L, and YCB-V coverage are retained. V2 adds a YCB-V scenario using rendered reference images, extending evaluation to synthetic reference inputs while retaining the same objects and reference poses.

E2.justification: Tables 1 and 2 retain the same segmentation and pose comparators, including CNOS, SAM-6D, FreeZe, UTOPIC, and the geometric-feature methods. Table 5 retains its existing comparison alternatives; the added rows are UNOPose ablation configurations.

E3.justification: V2 adds a controlled replacement of real references with pose-identical rendered references and a coarse-stage configuration with overlap prediction. Existing splits, reference-selection constraints, metrics, and training budgets remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Table 5 adds C2 to test overlap prediction without fine pose estimation and E0 to examine real versus rendered references. Existing GRF/LRF, segmentation, and reference-rotation analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report the same overlap-ratio means and standard deviations in Figure 3. V2 introduces no new repeated-run information, seeds, confidence intervals, significance tests, or uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: V2 adds Table 5 results for C2, with ARBOP 69.2, and rendered-reference E0, with ARBOP 85.5. The retained real-reference C1 scores 83.1, so E0 represents a different input condition. Previously reported results, including Table 2's 70.9 average, remain unchanged.

T1.justification: The supplied texts retain Equations 1–8, the GRF/LRF definitions, and the same invariance reasoning. No mathematical correction, new assumption, derivation, or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same novelty claims for single-unposed-reference pose estimation, the BOP-derived benchmark, and comparative performance against image-reference and CAD-based methods.

C2.justification: The new rendered-reference discussion attributes improved results to reduced depth noise and training–testing domain gap, while acknowledging the additional requirement for an object model. The existing limitation concerning extreme two-view geometry is unchanged.

D1.justification: V2 replaces the future code/data-release promise with an availability statement and repository link. It also explicitly documents identical query-reference pairs across comparison methods and clarifies the training role of SAM-6D's canonical templates. These disclosures do not establish changes to the existing experiments.

R1.justification: V2 adds citations including SecondPose, GPV-Pose, BlenderProc2, and GFreeDet, and removes Lin et al.'s 2022 self-supervised deep prior deformation paper. These changes expand supporting references without substantially changing the related-work narrative or UNOPose's positioning.

P1.justification: V2 locally tightens wording, abbreviates some descriptions, changes supplementary-material references to appendix references, and adds acknowledgements. Most prose and the section sequence remain intact.

P2.justification: V2 compresses spacing, relocates retained tables, and resizes and repositions Figure 3. Table 5 gains two rows and a reference-type caption extension. The existing diagrams, qualitative examples, and plot content are retained.

improvement.justification: The added coarse-stage overlap control and pose-matched rendered-reference experiment provide useful, limited evidence about the existing design and its input sensitivity. Clearer comparison pairing and code/data access information improve reproducibility documentation. The main method and benchmark results remain unchanged, and the rendered-reference benefit is appropriately qualified by its CAD-model requirement. Referenced appendix material remains unavailable for comparison.
